risk.instructions: This is a numbered slice of source code from an iPad teaching whiteboard app. Does the code shown contain a likely runtime defect? Judge only the code shown. Ignore style, naming and comments.

criteria.defect: a specific line can crash, lose or corrupt user data, race between threads, leak, or produce a wrong result under realistic input
criteria.fragile: no definite defect, but it depends on an unchecked assumption: force unwrap, unchecked index, swallowed error, unsynchronized shared state, missing cleanup
criteria.sound: inputs and errors are handled; nothing here is likely to misbehave

kind.instructions: If this code were to fail at runtime, which failure is most likely? Pick by the riskiest line shown.

criteria.crash: force unwrap, out-of-range index, division by zero, unexpected nil, fatalError
criteria.data_loss: file write, save, delete, move, migration or sync that can drop or overwrite user content
criteria.concurrency: shared mutable state touched from more than one thread, actor or queue; main-thread violations
criteria.lifecycle: observer, timer, task, web view or resource not released or torn down; retain cycle
criteria.logic: wrong condition, off-by-one, stale state, wrong unit or coordinate, unhandled case

pinpoint.instructions: Is there one specific numbered line in this code that misbehaves under a realistic input or timing? Answer yes only if you could name the line and the triggering condition.

criteria.yes: a nameable line fails for a nameable realistic condition: nil value, empty collection, missing file, failed write, re-entrant call, background thread, rotated or zero-size view
criteria.no: no single line can be named, or the failure needs an unrealistic condition
